intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

experiences.name: Authentic Korean BBQ Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a classic Korean BBQ dinner at one of Mapo-gu's legendary charcoal grill restaurants, famous for their premium samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs). Grill your own meat tableside, wrap it in fresh perilla leaves and lettuce, and pair it with an array of banchan (side dishes) and a glass of soju or makgeolli. This communal dining ritual is central to Korean social culture and an unmissable culinary highlight.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong Station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) or a 24-hour pojangmacha (street food tent) near Bupyeong Market.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Convenience store meal or instant ramen at the hotel — budget ₩3,000–6,000

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a T-money card at the airport or Bupyeong Station convenience store (₩2,500 deposit + load ₩20,000–30,000). This card is essential for all subway and bus travel. Keep receipts for budget tracking. Dress warmly — temperatures will be around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free hotel breakfast if included, then explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and the underground shopping arcade near Bupyeong Station — one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse affordable K-fashion and accessories. Walk to Bupyeong Traditional Market (부평전통시장) to soak in local daily life and pick up cheap snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Incheon Line 1) to Dongmyo or transfer to Seoul Line 1 toward Namdaemun Market in central Seoul. Spend the afternoon exploring Namdaemun Market (남대문시장), Korea's largest traditional market. Browse street food, clothing, accessories, and souvenirs. Visit nearby Deoksugung Palace (덕수궁) — entry ₩1,000 — and watch the traditional Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony (held at 11:00 and 14:00).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong (명동) for evening street food and K-culture shopping. Try tteokbokki, hotteok, and Korean fried chicken skewers from street stalls. Browse K-beauty shops like Innisfree, Etude House, and The Face Shop for affordable skincare. Return to hotel via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store kimbap — ₩1,500–3,000
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market street food: gimbap, sundae, or hotteok — ₩3,000–6,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food stalls: tteokbokki, corn dogs, skewers — ₩5,000–8,000

day_by_day.notes: Deoksugung Palace is free with the Gyeongbokgung combo ticket if you plan ahead. Myeongdong street food vendors are cash-preferred. Wear layers — it will be cold but manageable with proper clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3). Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — entry ₩3,000. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) near the palace gates for ₩10,000–15,000/hour and get free entry to the palace while wearing it. Explore the grand palace grounds, Geunjeongjeon throne hall, and the scenic Hyangwonjeong pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌한옥마을) — completely free. Stroll through the narrow alleys lined with traditional Korean hanok houses. Continue to Insadong (인사동) for traditional crafts, tea houses, and K-culture souvenirs. Visit Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex with indie shops and street performances.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's evening atmosphere and dine at a local Korean restaurant. Head back toward Bupyeong via subway. Stop at a local supermarket (Homeplus or E-Mart near Bupyeong) to stock up on snacks and drinks for the room.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Insadong traditional snacks: hotteok, dalgona candy, or a set meal at a local restaurant — ₩6,000–9,000
meals.dinner: Insadong or Anguk area: sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) or bibimbap at a local eatery — ₩7,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Hanbok rental is highly recommended for the Instagram-worthy experience and free palace entry. Bukchon Hanok Village is a residential area — please be respectful and quiet. Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (홍대) area — the heart of Korean youth culture, K-pop, and indie music. Explore Hongdae's street art murals, quirky cafes, and the famous Hongdae Free Market area (weekends are busier but weekday mornings are peaceful). Visit the Trick Eye Museum or Line Friends Store for K-culture immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Sinchon (신촌) and Ewha Womans University area — great for affordable shopping and street food. Browse the Ewha shopping street for budget K-fashion. Head to the nearby Han River (한강) Mapo area — Mangwon Hangang Park — for a scenic winter riverside walk. Rent a convenience store snack and enjoy the view.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the vibrant Friday night street performance scene. Watch buskers and K-pop cover dance groups perform for free near Hongdae Exit 9. Explore the night market and grab affordable Korean fried chicken (chimaek) at a local hof (pub).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Bupyeong convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Ewha or Sinchon area: tteokbokki set or kimbap + ramen combo — ₩5,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae: Korean fried chicken + beer (chimaek) at a local hof — ₩12,000–18,000 (splurge-worthy Friday treat)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is most lively on Friday and Saturday evenings. Street performances are free and start around 18:00–19:00. The Han River is very cold in December — bring a thermos with hot tea or coffee.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Dongdaemun (동대문). Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — exterior is free and architecturally stunning. Explore the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. Browse the massive Dongdaemun wholesale fashion markets (Doota, Migliore) which are great for budget K-fashion finds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a must for food lovers: try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Explore the fabric and vintage clothing sections. Walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) — a beautiful urban stream perfect for a peaceful winter stroll — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dongdaemun Night Market — the area comes alive after dark with street food and shopping. Many wholesale fashion stores open late (until 05:00). Browse for affordable K-fashion pieces. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market: bindaetteok + mayak gimbap + sikhye (rice drink) — ₩6,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun street food or a local Korean BBQ restaurant (samgyeopsal) — ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is extremely popular — go early for lunch to avoid the biggest crowds. Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully lit at night. Dongdaemun wholesale markets are best for bulk buying but individual items are also available.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon (이태원) and walk up to Namsan Mountain (남산). Take the Namsan Cable Car (₩9,500 round trip) or hike up the free walking trail (about 40 minutes). Visit N Seoul Tower (남산서울타워) — observation deck entry ₩21,000 but the outdoor plaza and love locks are free. Enjoy panoramic views of Seoul in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Namsan and explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood. Browse the antique shops and vintage stores along Antique Furniture Street. Visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) near Samgakji Station — entry is FREE and offers deep insight into Korean history and culture. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the extensive exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market (용산전자상가) near Yongsan Station for browsing the latest Korean tech and electronics. Grab dinner in the Yongsan area before heading back to Bupyeong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Itaewon area: affordable Korean-fusion or a local Korean restaurant — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Yongsan area: dosirak (Korean lunch box) restaurant or a local gukbap (rice soup) place — ₩7,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is one of Seoul's best free attractions — highly recommended. N Seoul Tower observation deck can be skipped to save money as the outdoor views are already great. Dress in very warm layers for Namsan — wind chill makes it feel much colder.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성). Take the subway from Bupyeong to Suwon Station (about 1 hour, ₩1,850 on T-money). Walk to Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Entry to the fortress walls is ₩1,000. Walk the full 5.7km fortress wall circuit for stunning winter views of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (행궁) — entry ₩1,500. Visit the nearby Paldalmun Gate and the traditional Suwon Jidong Market. Try the famous Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs) — Suwon is nationally renowned for this dish. Browse the traditional market for local snacks and produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong by subway. Rest and recover at the hotel. Pick up dinner from a local restaurant near Bupyeong Station or the hotel area. Explore Bupyeong's local neighborhood streets for a low-key evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Suwon Jidong Market: local street food and snacks — ₩5,000–8,000
meals.dinner: Suwon galbi at a local restaurant near Suwon Station (splurge) or Bupyeong local eatery — ₩12,000–20,000

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is one of Korea's most underrated UNESCO sites and very manageable as a day trip from Bupyeong. The fortress walk takes about 2 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear very warm shoes as the fortress walls are exposed to wind.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Anguk Station and visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) — entry ₩3,000. This UNESCO-listed palace is famous for its beautiful Secret Garden (Huwon). Book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (₩8,000 extra) — tours run at set times and are limited. The garden is magical even in winter with bare trees and stone pathways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) — entry ₩1,000 — connected to Changdeokgung. Explore the palace grounds and the traditional botanical greenhouse. Head to Jongno 3-ga area and visit Tapgol Park (탑골공원) — free — a historic park with a beautiful 10-story pagoda. Explore the Pimatgol alley (피맛골) area for traditional Korean street food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Jongno's Gwanghwamun Square (광화문광장) — free — beautifully lit during winter. See the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin. Enjoy the festive winter atmosphere and any seasonal light installations. Grab dinner in the Jongno area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Jongno area: seolleongtang (ox bone soup) or doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Pimatgol alley: traditional Korean pojangmacha food — ₩7,000–10,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour online at the official palace website well in advance as spots fill up quickly. Changdeokgung is closed on Mondays — today is Tuesday so it's open. Gwanghwamun Square may have special winter/Christmas decorations.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Gangnam (강남) — the upscale district made famous by PSY's 'Gangnam Style.' Visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰) — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Explore the stunning Starfield Library inside COEX — completely free and a beautiful K-culture photo spot. Browse the mall's shops and entertainment options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — free entry — a beautiful Buddhist temple sitting in contrast to the modern Gangnam skyline. Participate in a free temple tour if available. Head to Garosu-gil (가로수길) — a tree-lined street with indie boutiques, cafes, and K-culture shops. Window shop and enjoy the aesthetic street atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Apgujeong Rodeo Street (압구정 로데오) — the birthplace of Korean plastic surgery culture and high-end K-fashion. Browse the area and spot K-pop agency buildings (SM Entertainment is nearby). Return to Bupyeong for dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: COEX food court: various Korean options — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Bupyeong local restaurant: samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) or budae jjigae (army stew) — ₩9,000–13,000

day_by_day.notes: Gangnam is expensive for shopping but free to explore. The Starfield Library is one of Seoul's most Instagrammable spots. Bongeunsa Temple offers a peaceful contrast to the busy Gangnam district. Budget travelers should resist shopping temptations in Gangnam.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks. Entry is ₩62,000 for adults (splurge day) or explore the free Magic Island outdoor area and Lotte World Mall for free. Alternatively, visit the nearby Seokchon Lake (석촌호수) — completely free — beautifully decorated for Christmas with lights and installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jamsil area: visit the Lotte World Tower Sky31 observation deck (₩27,000) for incredible city views, or save money and admire the tower from outside. Walk around Seokchon Lake's full circuit (about 2.5km) enjoying the festive winter atmosphere. Visit the Olympic Park (올림픽공원) nearby — free entry — with outdoor sculptures and peaceful winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Seoul's Christmas Eve atmosphere in Myeongdong or Hongdae — both areas are beautifully decorated and buzzing with festive energy. Watch street performances, enjoy Christmas market-style street food, and soak in the K-culture Christmas experience. This is a special evening — enjoy it!

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Jamsil area: local Korean restaurant or food court — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special: Myeongdong or Hongdae street food feast + a warm cup of Korean traditional tea (sikhye or yujacha) — ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major event — streets will be very crowded and festive. Many couples celebrate Christmas Eve as a romantic holiday in Korea. Book any restaurant reservations in advance if you want a sit-down dinner. The city will be beautifully lit.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day in Seoul! Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul — free entry. The temple is beautifully decorated with colorful lanterns year-round. Attend a morning ceremony if interested. Walk through the surrounding Insadong area which is quieter on Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) for a winter hiking experience — entry is free. Take the subway to Gupabal Station and hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail (about 2–3 hours round trip). The winter mountain scenery with snow-dusted peaks is spectacular. This is a quintessential Korean outdoor experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and celebrate Christmas evening Korean-style with samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a local BBQ restaurant — a beloved Korean social dining experience. Toast with soju (₩1,500/bottle) and enjoy the communal atmosphere. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: Pack convenience store kimbap and snacks for the hike — ₩3,000–5,000
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ: samgyeopsal + soju at a local restaurant — ₩12,000–18,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check weather and trail conditions before hiking Bukhansan in winter — some trails may be icy. Bring hiking poles if possible and wear non-slip shoes. The hike is moderately challenging but very rewarding. Many restaurants will be open on Christmas Day in Korea as it's not a major dining holiday.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) near Ichon Station — entry is FREE. One of Asia's largest museums with incredible collections of Korean artifacts, pottery, Buddhist art, and historical exhibits. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the permanent collection. The museum grounds are also beautiful for a winter walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관) inside Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds — free entry. Explore exhibits on traditional Korean daily life, customs, and folk culture. This is perfect for K-culture enthusiasts. Walk through the palace grounds one more time to appreciate the winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Seoul — head to Lotte Mart or E-Mart for souvenir shopping: Korean snacks, instant ramen, K-beauty products, and traditional teas make great budget gifts. Return to Bupyeong and have a farewell dinner at a local restaurant you've been wanting to try.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — ₩2,000–4,000
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria or nearby restaurant — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Bupyeong local favorite: haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) + makgeolli (rice wine) at a traditional restaurant — ₩10,000–15,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is one of Seoul's absolute best free attractions — don't miss it. Saturday will be busy so arrive early. For souvenirs, supermarkets like Lotte Mart offer much better prices than tourist shops. Pack purchases carefully to avoid overweight baggage fees.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Incheon/Seoul. Check out of the hotel (standard checkout is 10:00 — confirm with hotel). Store luggage at the hotel or Bupyeong Station lockers. Take a final stroll through Bupyeong Market for last-minute snacks and souvenirs. Enjoy a proper Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head to Incheon International Airport via AREX (Airport Railroad Express) from Bupyeong or Seoul Station. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute K-beauty and snack purchases (often cheaper than city shops).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of K-culture, local food, and cultural exploration in Seoul and Incheon!

meals.breakfast: Local Korean breakfast restaurant near hotel: haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee — ₩6,000–9,000
meals.lunch: Bupyeong Market street food or airport food court — ₩8,000–12,000
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: AREX from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 40–60 minutes depending on the route. Check your specific flight time and work backward to plan your airport arrival. Use remaining T-money card balance at convenience stores before leaving — the card can be refunded at airport customer service centers (₩500 fee). Keep all receipts for final budget tallying.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or a limousine bus to Bupyeong station area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) or a 24-hour pojangmacha (street food tent) near Bupyeong Market.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snacks or instant ramen — try CU or GS25 near the hotel for Korean-style cup noodles, kimbap, and triangle gimbap (around ₩3,000–₩6,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Exchange some currency at the airport (Travelex or KEB Hana Bank kiosks). Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip. Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely start, explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall (underground shopping complex connected to Bupyeong Station) and the surrounding Bupyeong Market area. Get a feel for local Incheon neighborhood life and pick up any essentials you may need.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Sinchon or Hongdae area in Seoul (approx. 50–60 min). Explore Hongdae's vibrant street art, indie shops, and K-culture scene. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or just wander the lively streets filled with K-pop merchandise stores, vintage clothing shops, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Hongdae nightlife atmosphere. Browse K-pop idol merchandise shops and listen to buskers performing near Hongdae Park. Head back to Bupyeong by 21:00–22:00 via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery — try Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for coffee and pastries (₩5,000–₩8,000)
meals.lunch: Bupyeong Market street food — try sundae (blood sausage), tteokbokki, and hotteok (sweet pancake) from market stalls (₩5,000–₩10,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae area — try Yoogane Dak Galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or a Korean BBQ spot for samgyeopsal (pork belly). Budget around ₩15,000–₩25,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers and a warm coat. Hongdae is very walkable but can be cold in December. The subway ride from Bupyeong to Hongdae is straightforward on Line 1 (transfer at Digital Media City or direct routes available).

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Gyeongbokgung Palace (approx. 1 hour from Bupyeong via subway Line 1 to Jonggak, then Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung). Arrive early (opens 09:00) to watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop for free or discounted palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the narrow alleys and enjoy panoramic views of the city. Then visit Insadong, Seoul's cultural arts district, for galleries, traditional craft shops, and unique souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard complex for indie shops and local art. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights. Head back to Bupyeong via subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Insadong area — try Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup, ₩17,000) or a traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) at a local restaurant
meals.dinner: Insadong or Anguk area — try a cozy Korean restaurant for doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) and banchan (side dishes). Budget ₩12,000–₩20,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rentals near the palace cost around ₩10,000–₩20,000 for 2 hours. Bring hand warmers — it will be cold standing outside for the guard ceremony.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) via cable car from Myeong-dong. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck. See the famous love locks on the fence surrounding the tower. The tower opens at 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Myeong-dong, Seoul's premier shopping and street food district. Browse cosmetics shops (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young) for K-beauty products. Explore the bustling street food stalls along the main pedestrian street.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeong-dong for dinner and evening shopping. The area is beautifully lit during December. Visit명동성당 (Myeong-dong Cathedral), one of Korea's most iconic Catholic churches, which looks stunning with Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store
meals.lunch: Myeong-dong street food — try egg bread (계란빵), tornado potato, Korean fried chicken skewers, and hotteok. Budget ₩8,000–₩15,000 for a satisfying street food lunch.
meals.dinner: Myeong-dong — try Myeongdong Kyoja for their famous kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution. Budget ₩10,000–₩14,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car costs around ₩9,500 round trip. Observatory entry is ₩21,000. Myeong-dong is very crowded on weekends — Friday evening will be busy. Olive Young is great for affordable K-beauty shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Seoul's most beautiful palaces, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance (limited spots, tours run at set times).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), the futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun Market area. Browse the massive fabric and fashion wholesale markets nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun is famous for its late-night shopping — many stores open until 05:00. Enjoy the illuminated DDP exterior and explore the outdoor market stalls. Great for K-fashion finds at wholesale prices.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery café
meals.lunch: Near Changdeokgung — try a traditional Korean restaurant in the Anguk/Ikseon-dong area for bibimbap or a set lunch (₩12,000–₩18,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — try Gwangjang Market (a short subway ride away) for bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget ₩10,000–₩20,000.

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked online in advance at the official palace website. Tours are conducted in Korean and English. Gwangjang Market is one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets — a must for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a trendy neighborhood of converted hanok houses turned into cafés, boutiques, and restaurants. This is a more local, less touristy alternative to Bukchon. Perfect for a slow Sunday morning with coffee and pastries in a traditional setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (free entry to permanent collection). One of Asia's largest museums, it houses over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon Dynasty. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Itaewon for a multicultural evening experience. Explore the diverse restaurant scene and browse unique shops. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art area or simply enjoy the international atmosphere of this cosmopolitan neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Ikseon-dong café — try a specialty coffee and Korean-style brunch at one of the charming hanok cafés (₩8,000–₩15,000)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria or a nearby restaurant in Yongsan for a simple Korean meal (₩10,000–₩15,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon — try a Korean-fusion restaurant or explore the diverse dining options. Vatos Urban Tacos (Korean-Mexican fusion) or a traditional Korean BBQ spot. Budget ₩20,000–₩35,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Ikseon-dong is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid crowds — Sunday may be busy but still enjoyable. Itaewon has excellent English-language menus throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (approx. 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway). This UNESCO World Heritage fortress was built in the late 18th century and offers a scenic 5.7km walk along its walls. The winter morning light on the stone walls is beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon Hwaseong — visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (the temporary palace within the fortress walls) and the surrounding traditional market area. Take the fortress wall walk for panoramic views of Suwon city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Enjoy a relaxed evening near the hotel. Visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for some affordable Korean fashion and accessories.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — Suwon is famous for this dish. Try a local galbi restaurant near the fortress for an authentic regional specialty. Budget ₩20,000–₩30,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Near Bupyeong hotel — try a local Korean restaurant for sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) or doenjang jjigae with rice. Budget ₩8,000–₩12,000.

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress entry is ₩1,000. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Dress very warmly — walking along the exposed fortress walls in December can be very cold and windy. Bring hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan (free entry). This impressive museum documents Korea's military history with extensive indoor and outdoor exhibits, including aircraft, tanks, and artillery. Very informative for understanding modern Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam district — explore the upscale Apgujeong and Cheongdam-dong areas, the heart of Korean luxury culture and K-pop industry. Visit SM Town COEX Artium, a K-pop entertainment complex with a museum, merchandise store, and hologram theater dedicated to SM Entertainment artists.
day_by_day.evening: Explore COEX Mall, one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls. Visit the famous Starfield Library inside COEX — a stunning public library with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves. Browse the mall's shops and food court.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Near the War Memorial — try a Korean army stew (budae jjigae) restaurant, a dish born from the Korean War era that blends Korean and American ingredients. Budget ₩12,000–₩18,000.
meals.dinner: COEX Mall food court or a restaurant in Gangnam — try Korean fried chicken (치킨) with beer (chimaek) at a local chain like BBQ Chicken or Kyochon. Budget ₩15,000–₩25,000.

day_by_day.notes: SM Town COEX Artium entry fees vary by experience. The Starfield Library is free and open to the public. Gangnam is more expensive than other districts — budget accordingly for shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, located in central Seoul. In December, the temple is beautifully decorated with colorful lanterns for the winter season. Explore the serene temple grounds and learn about Korean Buddhist culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream, a restored urban stream running through central Seoul. The 5.8km stream is a peaceful urban oasis and is beautifully lit during the winter. Walk along the stream toward Gwangjang Market for afternoon snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Gwangjang Market in the evening for a vibrant night market atmosphere. This is one of Seoul's best food markets — try multiple dishes from different stalls. The market is especially lively in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Near Jogyesa Temple — try a temple food restaurant for a unique Buddhist vegetarian meal experience (사찰음식). Budget ₩15,000–₩25,000.
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — feast on bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and soju. Budget ₩15,000–₩25,000 for a full market dinner experience.

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free to enter. The Cheonggyecheon Stream walk is free and very pleasant. December evenings are cold — the stream area can be windy, so dress warmly. Gwangjang Market is cash-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World, one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, located in Jamsil. Enjoy the festive Christmas Eve decorations and atmosphere. The indoor section is perfect for a cold December day. Alternatively, explore the adjacent Lotte World Mall and Lotte World Tower (123 floors).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seoul Sky Observatory at the top of Lotte World Tower (floors 117–123) for breathtaking panoramic views of Seoul. On a clear winter day, you can see for miles. The glass-floored observation deck is thrilling.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city is beautifully decorated. Head to Myeong-dong or Cheongdam-dong for Christmas Eve festivities, carol performances, and festive street food. Many churches hold special Christmas Eve services.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lotte World Mall food court — wide variety of Korean and international options. Budget ₩12,000–₩20,000.
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer Korean restaurant. Try a Korean BBQ restaurant for galbi (beef short ribs) and samgyeopsal. Budget ₩25,000–₩40,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World entry is ₩62,000 for adults (full day pass). Seoul Sky Observatory is ₩29,000. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very festive — the city embraces Christmas culture enthusiastically. Book dinner reservations in advance as restaurants will be busy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Hanok Village, a collection of restored traditional Korean houses at the foot of Namsan Mountain. The village showcases traditional Korean architecture and culture. Enjoy the peaceful atmosphere on Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Han River Parks (Yeouido Hangang Park or Banpo Hangang Park). In winter, the parks offer a serene, frost-covered landscape. Rent a bicycle or simply walk along the river. The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain may operate on weekends.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Yeouido for the Christmas evening atmosphere. Visit the IFC Mall or Times Square Mall for holiday shopping and dining. Enjoy the festive city lights as you make your way back to Bupyeong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a relaxed Christmas morning
meals.lunch: Near Namsan Hanok Village — try a traditional Korean restaurant for a hearty Christmas lunch. Galbitang (beef short rib soup) or seolleongtang (ox bone soup) are perfect for a cold winter day. Budget ₩12,000–₩18,000.
meals.dinner: Yeouido area — try a Korean restaurant for a Christmas dinner. Many restaurants offer special holiday menus. Budget ₩20,000–₩35,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Most major attractions and restaurants remain open. Public transportation runs on a holiday schedule. The Han River parks are beautiful but very cold — dress in your warmest layers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea, located within the Gyeongbokgung Palace grounds (separate entry). This museum provides an excellent overview of traditional Korean folk culture, customs, and daily life through the ages. Very relevant for K-culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood, often called 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' This former industrial area has been transformed into a hub of artisan cafés, design studios, vintage shops, and creative spaces. Very popular with young Koreans and a great insight into contemporary Korean culture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Lotte Mart or E-Mart near Bupyeong for last-minute Korean food souvenirs — dried seaweed, instant ramyeon, Korean snacks, gochujang paste, and K-beauty products. Pack your purchases and prepare for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Seongsu-dong — try one of the trendy cafés or a local Korean restaurant. The area is known for artisan coffee and creative food. Budget ₩12,000–₩20,000.
meals.dinner: Near Bupyeong hotel — try a local Korean BBQ restaurant for a farewell dinner. Enjoy samgyeopsal (pork belly) with soju and makgeolli (rice wine). Budget ₩20,000–₩30,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot. The area has many Instagram-worthy spots and is a great place to see modern Korean creative culture. Saturday will be busy — arrive at popular cafés early to avoid long waits.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last walk around the Bupyeong neighborhood and Bupyeong Market for any final souvenir shopping or street food you may have missed. Pick up Korean snacks, instant noodles, and local specialties to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head to Incheon International Airport. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) from Bupyeong or a nearby station. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in, immigration, and security. Browse the duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute K-beauty and Korean food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring Seoul's rich K-culture, incredible food scene, and fascinating history.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy your last Korean hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Bupyeong Market street food for a final taste of local Korean street food, or airport food court at Incheon (budget ₩10,000–₩20,000)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Incheon Airport has excellent duty-free shopping and dining. Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a ₩500 card deposit). The airport has a Korean Cultural Street on the departure level with traditional performances and cultural exhibits — worth a look if time permits.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight is late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into the hotel. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its night food scene)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — prioritize rest. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance. Keep Day 2 morning light to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start to recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, then take a short walk around Bupyeong district to get oriented. Visit Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for a quick browse — one of Korea's largest underground malls, great for warming up on a cold December morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway from Bupyeong to explore Incheon's Chinatown and Jayu Park — a short, scenic introduction to Korean-Chinese culture. Walk along the colorful murals of Sinpo International Market and pick up local street snacks like hotteok (sweet pancakes) and tteokbokki to warm up.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market area for dinner. Return to hotel early for a good night's rest before the full Seoul itinerary begins.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café
meals.lunch: Sinpo International Market street food — jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at a traditional Incheon Chinatown restaurant such as Gonghwachun, one of Korea's oldest Chinese restaurants
meals.dinner: Premium Korean BBQ at a local Bupyeong restaurant — try Hanwoo (Korean beef) at a well-regarded local grill house near Bupyeong station

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation day. Keep pace relaxed. Temperatures will be around 3°C — dress in warm layers. Bupyeong subway station (Line 1 & 7) is your main transit hub.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul (approx. 50–60 min by subway). Begin with the Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience — arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Rent a premium Hanbok from a nearby rental shop (Gyeongbokgung Hanbok rental shops open from 9:00 AM) and explore the stunning 14th-century palace grounds in traditional dress. Visit Gyeonghoeru Pavilion and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the winding alleys, admire the architecture, and stop at a traditional tea house for warm yujacha (citron tea). Visit a premium Korean craft shop for high-quality souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Cultural Village for an evening exploration. Browse the eclectic galleries, antique shops, and artisan boutiques. Enjoy a premium dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Café near Gyeongbokgung — try Café Bora (famous for purple taro soft-serve and Korean-style pastries)
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) at Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — famous for its ginseng chicken soup, perfect for cold weather
meals.dinner: Premium Korean cuisine at Jungsik or a high-end traditional restaurant in Insadong — try a multi-course Korean dinner featuring seasonal winter ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — Thursday is perfect. Hanbok rental is included in the experience. Wear thermal underlayers as you'll be outdoors most of the day in sub-zero temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration in the morning when it's quieter. Wander through Ssamziegil — a unique open-air shopping complex with indie boutiques and artisan stalls. Explore traditional paper (hanji) shops, pottery galleries, and calligraphy studios. Stop at a traditional tea house for a ceremonial tea experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Jogyesa Temple — Seoul's most important Buddhist temple, beautifully decorated with lanterns in winter. Then head to Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) for a guided tour — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building, beautifully lit at night. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district and night markets.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a hanok café in Insadong — doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) with rice and banchan
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Changdeokgung — try naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbi-tang (short rib soup) at Woo Lae Oak, a Seoul institution
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant near DDP — try modern Korean fusion at Mingles or a high-end Korean BBQ restaurant in the Dongdaemun area

day_by_day.notes: Book the Changdeokgung Secret Garden tour in advance — English tours are limited. DDP is spectacular at night with its LED light installations.

day_by_day.morning: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — Saturday is the perfect day to experience this iconic market at its liveliest. Arrive around 9:30–10:00 AM. Taste bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and freshly made mandu (dumplings). Take a guided food tour for the full insider experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Walk along the elevated pathway and enjoy the winter scenery. Continue to Myeongdong for premium Korean skincare and cosmetics shopping at flagship stores (Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, Innisfree).
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower on Namsan Mountain — take the cable car up for panoramic night views of Seoul. Attach a love lock on the fence and enjoy the romantic winter atmosphere. Dinner in the Myeongdong or Namsan area.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast at Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok and mayak gimbap with sikhye (sweet rice drink)
meals.lunch: Continue grazing at Gwangjang Market or sit-down lunch at a nearby traditional Korean restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at N Grill restaurant inside N Seoul Tower — fine dining with panoramic Seoul views (reservation required)

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends — arrive early to avoid the largest crowds. Book N Grill well in advance. The cable car to Namsan operates until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — one of Korea's most unique and historically significant experiences. Book a premium guided DMZ tour departing from central Seoul. Visit the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, and Dora Observatory for views into North Korea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the DMZ tour — visit Dorasan Station (the last train station before North Korea) and the Imjingak Peace Park. Return to Seoul by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover from the day trip. Explore the upscale Gangnam district in the evening — visit COEX Mall (one of Asia's largest underground malls) and the stunning COEX Starfield Library.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the DMZ tour departure
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the premium DMZ tour package or at a restaurant near Imjingak
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Gangnam — try Gaon (three Michelin stars, traditional Korean royal cuisine) or Kwon Sooksoo for an elevated Korean dining experience

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours require passport and advance booking — book at least 2–3 days ahead. The JSA tour requires additional security clearance. Dress warmly as the DMZ area is very exposed and cold.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World Tower — take the elevator to the Seoul Sky observation deck on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking 360-degree views of Seoul. The glass-floored Sky Bridge is spectacular on a clear winter morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jamsil and the surrounding Songpa district. Visit Lotte World — Asia's largest indoor theme park — for a few hours of entertainment. Alternatively, stroll along the scenic Seokchon Lake surrounding the park, beautifully lit in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the trendy Seongsu-dong district — Seoul's 'Brooklyn' — for an evening of gallery hopping, artisan coffee, and boutique shopping in converted industrial spaces.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a premium café near Lotte World Tower — try Café de Paris or a high-end brunch spot in Jamsil
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant inside Lotte World Mall — Korean or international cuisine at one of the upscale dining options
meals.dinner: Dinner in Seongsu-dong — try Onion (a beloved artisan bakery and café) for coffee and pastries, followed by dinner at a trendy Seongsu restaurant such as Dosa or a modern Korean bistro

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Sky observation deck tickets should be booked online in advance to avoid queues. Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: K-Pop Idol Dance Class in Hongdae — take the subway to Hongdae (Hongik University area), Seoul's vibrant youth and arts district. Attend a 2-hour K-Pop dance class at one of Hongdae's dedicated academies (such as 1MILLION Dance Studio or K-Pop dance schools offering tourist classes). Learn choreography from iconic K-Pop songs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae's street art, indie music scene, and unique shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or the LINE Friends flagship store. Browse the eclectic boutiques and vintage shops along Hongdae's main streets.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening — experience the famous Hongdae street performances and nightlife. Visit a premium cocktail bar or rooftop lounge.

meals.breakfast: Artisan café breakfast in Hongdae — try Fritz Coffee Company, one of Seoul's most celebrated specialty coffee roasters
meals.lunch: Lunch at a popular Hongdae restaurant — try Maple Tree House for premium Korean BBQ or a trendy Korean fusion spot
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium Hongdae restaurant — try Yardbird Seoul for Korean-inspired rotisserie chicken or a high-end izakaya-style restaurant in the area

day_by_day.notes: Book the K-Pop dance class in advance — tourist-friendly classes fill up quickly. Wear comfortable athletic clothing for the dance class. Hongdae is very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning hike — one of the world's most visited national parks located within a major city. Take the trail to Baegundae Peak or a shorter scenic route for stunning winter mountain views over Seoul. The snow-dusted granite peaks in December are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the upscale Hannam-dong district — Seoul's most exclusive neighborhood. Browse the luxury boutiques, international galleries, and designer concept stores along Itaewon-ro and the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon — Seoul's most international district — for a cosmopolitan evening. Visit the premium cocktail bars and restaurants along Itaewon's main strip and the trendy Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near the Bukhansan trailhead — traditional Korean porridge (juk) at a local restaurant to fuel the hike
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch in Hannam-dong — try Vatos Urban Tacos (Korean-Mexican fusion) or a premium Korean restaurant in the area
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Itaewon — try Cote Korean Steakhouse or Bab (a celebrated modern Korean restaurant) for a world-class dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan trails can be icy in December — bring hiking poles and wear trail shoes with good grip. The park is free to enter. Hannam-dong is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Deoksugung Palace — the only royal palace in Seoul where you can watch the traditional Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony (held at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM). The palace is beautifully decorated for the winter season. Walk along Deoksugung Stonewall Walkway — one of Seoul's most romantic paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Seoul City Hall Plaza — beautifully decorated with Christmas lights and ice skating rink for the holiday season. Skate on the outdoor rink or simply enjoy the festive atmosphere. Visit the Seoul Museum of History nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city is beautifully lit with holiday decorations. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the Christmas Eve mass (a beautiful experience even for non-religious visitors). Enjoy the festive street atmosphere in Myeongdong.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel-style breakfast or brunch at a café near Deoksugung
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near City Hall — try Balwoo Gongyang, a celebrated temple food restaurant near Jogyesa Temple
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a top Seoul restaurant — try La Yeon (three Michelin stars, traditional Korean cuisine at The Shilla Hotel) or Pierre Gagnaire à Séoul for a memorable festive dinner (reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a major celebration in Seoul — book dinner reservations weeks in advance. The city is beautifully decorated and very lively. Myeongdong Cathedral mass is a unique cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely Christmas morning. Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace — a lesser-known but beautiful royal palace, usually less crowded. Explore the adjacent Seoul Museum of History for a deep dive into Seoul's fascinating urban history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Apgujeong and Cheongdam-dong districts — Seoul's most exclusive luxury shopping area. Browse flagship stores of Korean luxury brands (MCM, Gentle Monster, Ader Error) and international luxury houses. Visit the Dior flagship store and the iconic Gentle Monster Haus Dosan concept store.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium Christmas dinner in Gangnam. Visit the festively decorated COEX area or Cheongdam-dong for after-dinner cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at the hotel or a premium brunch restaurant
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Apgujeong restaurant — try Soigné (a celebrated modern Korean tasting menu restaurant) or a high-end café in the area
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at Jungsik (two Michelin stars, modern Korean cuisine) or Mosu Seoul for an unforgettable holiday dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions are open on Christmas Day in Seoul. Luxury shopping districts are busy but festive. Book all Christmas Day dining well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea — one of Asia's largest and most impressive military museums, with extensive outdoor exhibits of aircraft, tanks, and artillery. A deeply moving and educational experience covering Korea's complex military history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the scenic Han River (Hangang) — rent a bicycle or take a leisurely walk along the riverside park. Visit Yeouido Hangang Park and enjoy the winter scenery. Stop at the 63 Building observation deck for panoramic river views.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Seoul — return to Hongdae or Gangnam for a farewell dinner and evening of K-culture immersion. Visit a norebang (private karaoke room) for a quintessential Korean entertainment experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the War Memorial — traditional Korean breakfast at a local restaurant in Itaewon or Yongsan
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Yeouido — try a high-end Korean restaurant or the upscale dining options in the IFC Mall Yeouido
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a premium Korean BBQ restaurant — try Maple Tree House in Itaewon or Palsaik Samgyeopsal for a premium pork belly experience with eight different marinades

day_by_day.notes: The Han River parks are beautiful in winter but very cold — dress warmly. Norebang rooms can be booked by the hour and are a must-do Korean cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul/Incheon. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center or pick up Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts at a nearby convenience store or supermarket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if time allows, take a final stroll around Bupyeong or visit a nearby café. Begin packing and preparing for departure. Arrange private transfer back to Incheon International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy duty-free shopping at the airport — Incheon has one of the world's best airport shopping experiences with premium Korean brands and international luxury goods.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a premium café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Incheon Airport — try the premium Korean restaurant options in the departure terminal (Bibigo or a traditional Korean restaurant airside)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Incheon Airport at least 3 hours before international departure. The airport has excellent lounges (Korean Air KAL Lounge, Asiana Lounge) accessible with premium tickets or Priority Pass. Stock up on Korean snacks, instant ramyeon, and cosmetics at duty-free.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
